name: Kohima
description: Capital of Nagaland and headquarters of Kohima district, a scenic hill town at about 1,444 m elevation known for its Angami Naga culture, War Cemetery, and as the base for Hornbill Festival and surrounding highland attractions.
facts: Gateway to Dzukou Valley and Kisama
Host base for annual Hornbill Festival

name: Kohima War Cemetery
description: Commonwealth War Graves Commission cemetery on the site of the 1944 Battle of Kohima (Battle of the Tennis Court) on Garrison Hill. Contains 1,420 Commonwealth burials and a memorial to 917 cremated Hindu and Sikh soldiers; famous epitaph and preserved tennis court lines.
facts: Site of decisive 1944 Battle of Kohima
Famous epitaph: 'When you go home tell them of us and say for your tomorrow we gave our today'

name: Kisama Heritage Village (Naga Heritage Village)
description: Open-air cultural village between Kigwema and Phesama, 12 km south of Kohima, featuring morungs of Nagaland’s major tribes. Primary venue of the annual Hornbill Festival (December) showcasing Naga music, dance, crafts and cuisine.
facts: Venue of annual Hornbill Festival (1–10 December)
About 12 km south of Kohima on NH2
Name derived from Kigwema and Phesama villages

name: Khonoma Green Village
description: Western Angami Naga village 20 km west of Kohima, India’s first Green Village (declared 2005). Features terraced paddy fields, traditional architecture, Khonoma Fort, and the community-conserved Tragopan Sanctuary protecting Blyth’s Tragopan.
facts: Khonoma Nature Conservation and Tragopan Sanctuary

name: Dzukou Valley (Dzükou Valley)
description: High-altitude valley (about 2,438–2,452 m) on the Kohima–Senapati (Manipur) border, known as the Valley of Flowers of the Northeast for seasonal wildflowers including the endemic Dzukou lily, rolling meadows of dwarf bamboo, and popular multi-day treks.
facts: Famous for seasonal Dzukou lily and wildflowers

name: Japfu Peak (Mount Japfü)
description: Second-highest peak in Nagaland at 3,048 m in the Barail Range, about 15 km south of Kohima. Popular for sunrise treks; home to the world’s tallest rhododendron tree (Guinness record).
facts: World’s tallest rhododendron tree on slopes

name: Nagaland State Museum
description: State museum on Bayavü Hill, Kohima, opened 1970. Houses comprehensive ethnographic collections of Naga tribal artefacts, costumes, weapons, musical instruments, and cultural displays from across the state.
facts: Operated by Department of Art and Culture
Displays artefacts of all major Naga tribes

name: Mary Help of Christians Cathedral
description: Roman Catholic cathedral in Kohima, consecrated 1991, with architecture blending traditional Naga house elements. Features a large carved wooden crucifix; partly funded by Japanese donors in memory of soldiers who died in the Battle of Kohima.
facts: Architecture incorporates traditional Naga house facade
16-ft carved wooden crucifix among largest in Asia
Seat of the Roman Catholic Diocese of Kohima

name: Dzüleke Village
description: Remote Angami Naga eco-tourism village in western Kohima district (about 30–40 km from Kohima) at high elevation. Community-run homestays, hunting ban since 1999, mithun grazing, and streams with snowtrout; ideal for quiet nature and cultural stays.

name: Touphema Tourist Village
description: Community-run heritage tourist village about 36–41 km north of Kohima, recreating traditional Angami Naga architecture with cottages. Promotes Sekrenyi festival and offers cultural immersion, local cuisine, and short treks.
facts: Community initiative with state tourism support
